maya: heads-up — nodes gpu-ux-w1-12 and gpu-ux-w1-29 are spiking ECC errors; saw a burst of Xid12/Xid31 over the last 6h, a few jobs got requeued. logs attached to alert 😬

infra-oncall-bot: [ALERT] gpu-healthwatch: ECC_BURST on us-west1 (2 nodes). count=8 window=15m. ticket=INFRA-8421.

sam: can you paste the nvidia-smi excerpts? curious if temps or ECC only.

maya: quick paste from /var/log/nvml.log:
```
2026-03-17T02:11:23Z gpu-ux-w1-12 Xid=12 ECC=1 temp=72C Pstate=3
2026-03-17T02:15:02Z gpu-ux-w1-12 Xid=31 ECC=3 temp=73C Pstate=3
2026-03-17T07:02:11Z gpu-ux-w1-29 Xid=12 ECC=2 temp=69C Pstate=3
```

cheng: thanks. proposal: implement a "probe-handoff" orchestration instead of immediate hard cordon. Steps I suggest:
  1) Run 3 quick probes spaced 30s apart (nvml read + small CUDA memcpy) to avoid transient noise.
  2) If >=2 probes fail, transition node -> soft-cordon (k8s: taint + scheduling disabled for new pods but allow existing to finish).
  3) Trigger a quick Slurm-compatible probe job (srun --gres=gpu:1 --time=00:02:00 nvbench) that runs on the node to validate hardware under load.
  4) If probe fails, begin controlled drain: allow running jobs to checkpoint (grace=10m), mark NodeState=RESERVED in Slurm for evacuation, then hard drain/cordon and schedule replacement.
  5) If probe passes, clear soft-cordon and bump node healthscore with backoff.

sam: that sounds sensible. couple of questions:
  - how do we avoid mass-evict storms when many nodes blip simultaneously?
  - what about preemptible capacity and cost spikes if we instantly reschedule?

cheng: answers:
  - add zone-level rate-limit + randomized splay for cordon actions; target max concurrent cordons = ceil(total_gpus_zone * 0.03) and global limit 6 nodes.
  - capacity-aware deferral: if free_gpus_percent < 12% then escalate to manual review instead of auto hard-drain.

leah: cost note: if we fallback to on-demand/reserved capacity during mass drains we'll see a transient billing jump. add a smoothing window (30m) for auto-scaling so we don't spike instance churn. also add metric that tags drains that caused >5% on-demand bump.

maya: I'll draft the daemon behavior. rough pseudo-config for the probe flow:
```
{"probe_window_s":30, "probes":3, "probe_fail_threshold":2, "soft_cordon_grace_s":600, "zone_cordon_rate":0.03, "min_free_gpu_pct_for_auto":12}
```

maya: kubectl bits for k8s flow (for reference):
```
# soft cordon (allow running pods to finish)
kubectl taint node gpu-ux-w1-12 redteam/gpu-failing=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
# later, hard cordon + drain
drainctl cordon gpu-ux-w1-12 --evict --grace-period=600
```

sam: for Slurm hook I'll mirror the behavior: on soft-fail mark NodeState=RESERVED and add comment 'probe-fail:pending-checkpoint', then submit quick srun probe. if fails, set NodeState=DOWN, start reimage playbook. I'll open a PR for the slurm-hook.

infra-oncall-bot: Created ticket INFRA-8421 with linked runbook "probe-handoff-orch". Canary job submitted: gpu-probe-canary-17.

leah: add observability: metric names: gpu_probe.attempts, gpu_probe.failures, gpu_probe.handoff_count, gpu_drain.impact_on_on_demand. add trace tags: node, zone, probe_id.

maya: can someone own the first PR review? I'll start the daemon branch: gpu-probe/handoff. ping @cheng @sam for hooks. planning to include unit tests for hysteresis and a fake NVML probe. will post draft shortly. :rocket: 

sam: I'll pick up the Slurm hook PR review.

cheng: will review the daemon PR; we should also add an integration test in the lab cluster with a flaky card emulator before rollout.

maya: thanks all — keeping this thread as the working place until PRs land.
